observation.visible_scene: A tranquil outdoor landscape: a calm pond or slow river with a large leafless tree growing directly out of the water at the center, its trunk and bare branches mirrored in the surface. A long horizontal branch reaches leftward over the water. Golden-brown dry reeds/grass line the foreground banks, low hills rise on both sides, and a clear deep-blue sky fills the upper frame. The composition (tree position, hill outlines, horizon) stays fixed throughout, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: The water surface is not perfectly still: gentle ripples move across it, so the mirror reflection of the central tree and of the bright sky continuously distorts and reshapes from frame to frame (the dark reflected trunk and the bright reflected patches break into shifting wavy patterns).
No detectable translation, pan, or zoom of the camera; the tree, hills, and sky hold the same position relative to the frame edges from the first to the last sample.
The bare tree branches themselves show no discernible sway or deformation; the only visible motion is in the water and its reflection.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produces the water ripples (wind, current, or an unseen disturbance) is not shown.
Whether the foreground grass or any branch moves slightly is not confirmable within this short excerpt.
Events before t=0 and after t=2.67s are outside the cropped segment.
uncertain_details: Possible very subtle movement of the foreground reeds is not clearly resolvable between frames.
Any sub-pixel camera drift is too small to confirm against the static background.
